journeys.name: missing-state-is-refused-in-production
assertions: 401, not 502 — the exchange is never attempted
no user row is created, no shop provisioned, no credential persisted
the refusal names the missing state parameter

journeys.name: app-review-flow-is-not-broken-outside-production
journeys.entryUrl: the same callback with no state, ENVIRONMENT != production
assertions: the no-state path is still reachable, so TikTok app review keeps working

htmlRoutes: not-applicable: API-only change, no HTML route

migrationCompatibility.notes: No schema change. A guard on an existing route; the only behaviour change is that a production callback with no state is refused instead of provisioning.

rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: revert to the prior sha; the callback returns to accepting a stateless production callback, which is the defect this fixes

doNotInfer: Do not make the guard unconditional — TikTok's app-review callback carries no state, and refusing it everywhere breaks app review
Do not read this as closing the whole finding: the threat model still states 'State parameter validated' without recording the app-review exception
Do not re-use the Observation 2 attestation for the new sha — #1339 binds an attestation to the deployed sha, so boundary 1 must be re-probed after this deploys
